---
title: "6.13 Review of Count DVs"
---

- Linear regression is not advised for count outcomes
  - Limited options for interpretation
  - Incorrect standard errors / significance tests
- The Poisson is rarely the best fit to the data
  - The standard errors can sometimes be drastically off
  - Start with negative binomial and skip Poisson since you have to estimate the negative binomial model to test if Poisson is appropriate anyway
- Consider what it is you want to describe
  - Predicted rates are almost always of interest
  - Predicted probabilities of specific outcomes or of a range of outcomes are also often of interest
- Remember that the models are nonlinear and interactive
  - Sometimes effects (especially for the rate) will look relatively linear---but not always
- Zero inflated models do a good job of dealing with "excess" zeros
  - These can be very theoretically interesting models, allowing you to model two processes simultaneously
- There are good and reliable statistical tests for choosing the best fitting model
  - Consider the balance of parsimony and fit; BIC does this nicely
  - **countfit** / **countfit()** is useful and saves you a lot of time---performing all of the reasonable tests for you automatically
